answer: The protocol requires agents to store 1,000 unique data shards to ensure individual utility. A verifier emits a ripple effect by requesting unpredictable segments, forcing agents to demonstrate active custody. While an honest node bears a baseline storage cost, 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost as they maintain non-overlapping data in the digital willow grove. A meadow of audit threads checks for consistent proof-of-replication before rewarding tokens; failure to respond leads to immediate slashing of the capacity deposit without any refund, preventing collusion.
